title: The tenth man
hookLine: ten students count only nine, and a short poem of Shankara's says the Self is known, not earned
carry: the self is known, not earned
tomorrow: what's the one line under the whole year?
last: MISSING GOD IS A MARK OF BHAKTI.

cards: Ten students cross a river in flood. On the far bank, their leader counts to be sure everyone made it. One, two, three, all the way to nine.
He counts again: nine. Each of them takes a turn, and each one gets nine. So they sit on the bank and weep for the friend the river took.
A traveler stops, listens, and asks the leader to count once more. Seven, eight, nine. And the traveler taps him on the chest: you are the tenth.

teach.b: Advaita teachers have told that parable for centuries; Vidyaranya's Panchadashi uses it. Notice what the tenth man needed. Not a search party.
Not more effort. Nothing was lost. He only had to know.
That's the path of jnana, knowing, and a short Sanskrit poem called the Atmabodha, knowledge of the Self, puts it plainly.
Tradition gives it to Shankara, the great teacher of Advaita Vedanta; some scholars question whether he wrote it.

teach.h: ADVAITA: ATMAN AND BRAHMAN, NOT TWO.
teach.b: Advaita means not two: the deepest Self in you, the atman, and Brahman, the reality behind everything, are not two.

The poem's second verse: as fire is what actually cooks the food, knowledge, not any other practice, directly brings freedom. Verse three gives the reason. Action isn't opposed to ignorance, so it can't destroy it.
Knowledge is, the way light is opposed to darkness.

teach.h: KNOWLEDGE FREES, AS A LAMP ENDS DARK.
teach.b: Sweep a dark room all night; only a lamp ends the dark.

teach.h: LIKE THE SUN WHEN CLOUDS PASS.
teach.b: And verse four: through ignorance the Self seems small; when ignorance goes, it shines on its own, like the sun when the clouds pass.

teach.h: THE SELF IS KNOWN, NOT EARNED.
teach.b: So in this teaching you don't earn the Self, or build it, or fix it. It was never missing, any more than the tenth man was. That's the idea under the old line: you are not the body; you are atman.
Not every school agrees on the road. Shankara's holds that knowledge alone frees, with action and devotion readying the mind.
Ramanuja's tradition gives loving devotion to the Lord the central place, a knowing that has become love. Yesterday's gopis would like that.

how: In Advaita Vedanta circles, the Atmabodha is often among the first texts a student reads with a teacher, verse by verse, alongside listening, reflection and meditation; teachers often tell the tenth man along the way. Many students pair study like this with work done as service and with devotion.

o: the effort of good works that earns freedom
learning many facts about the sacred texts
knowing that frees, like light ending the dark

games.q: a friend asks: if the Self is already free, why does anyone study, pray or practice at all? by Shankara's teaching:
o: practice readies the mind; knowing is what frees, the lamp, not the sweeping.
there's no point; stop doing anything.
practice slowly builds a Self until it's finally free.
games.why: in Shankara's school, action and devotion prepare the mind, but only knowledge ends ignorance, the way only light ends the dark. nothing is built; something is seen.

practice: Sit still and let sounds, thoughts and feelings come and go. Then ask, quietly, the question Hindu teachers of self-inquiry give: who is noticing all this? Don't answer with a word.
Just turn toward the one who's aware, the way the leader finally counted himself. If you drift, that's fine; noticing the drift is part of it.

wordCard.voice: Jnana. Knowing, from the root to know. Not collecting facts: seeing what was there all along, like the tenth man.

orig.note: Sanskrit jñāna, knowing, from the root jñā, to know; the title Ātmabodha (आत्मबोध) means awakening to the Self.

carryVoice: Take this with you: the Self is known, not earned. You were the tenth all along. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Ramanuja's view of bhakti and knowledge (Vishishtadvaita), in general
